claims.text: After two proper courses fail, use another agent
claims.quote: After trials of two appropriately administered courses of permethrin, an alternative agent should be used.

claims.text: Malathion, spinosad and topical ivermectin kill eggs in one treatment. Permethrin, pyrethrins and benzyl alcohol don't, so repeat at seven to 10 days (nine is optimal)
claims.quote: Malathion, spinosad, and topical ivermectin are considered ovicidal, and they will kill both live lice and eggs in one treatment. Nonovicidal agents (permethrin, pyrethrins, benzyl alcohol, dimethicone, oral ivermectin, and isopropyl myristate) typically require a repeat application for complete eradication. Timing for nonovicidal treatments is based on the life cycle of the louse.19 An initial application followed by a second application seven to 10 days later (nine days is optimal)
